lines.text: In twenty seventeen, Robert Lewandowski got scammed.
He and his wife gave a hundred thousand zloty to save Antosh, a two-year-old boy with eye cancer.
More than six thousand other people gave too. Half a million zloty in total.
But Antosh never existed.
The organizer made him up, and spent the money on himself.
The Lewandowskis got their money back. Thousands of others never did.
In twenty seventeen, a fundraiser in Poland asked people to save Antosh, a two-year-old boy with eye cancer.
More than six and a half thousand people gave. Half a million zloty.
But Antosh never existed.
The organizer made him up, and spent the money on himself.
One famous donor got a refund. Thousands of others did not.
And it isn't only medical. Floods, wars, animal shelters: any good cause can be faked.
After the 2024 floods in Poland, police found a hundred and fifty fake fundraisers for the victims.
In the US, people reported losing ninety-six million dollars to fake charities and fundraisers in 2024 alone.
And that's only the people who reported it.
On most platforms, that money takes the same path.
From the donors, through the platform, into the organizer's own account.
After that, all you have is trust.
So we asked: what if the organizer could never touch the money at all?
With Earmark, donations wait in a vault that nobody holds the key to. Not the organizer. Not us.
It can only go to a verified recipient, like a clinic or a shelter, which confirms the need first.
When the target is reached, the money goes straight to the recipient.
If it isn't, every donor takes their own money back.
No middleman holding the money. Just rules in code that nobody can bend.
This is Earmark.
With Earmark, the money doesn't sit with a company. It waits in a vault on the Solana blockchain, and nobody holds its key. Not the organizer. Not us.
It can only go to a verified recipient, like a clinic or a shelter, which confirms the need first.
When the target is reached, the money goes straight to the recipient.
If it isn't, every donor takes their own money back.
Why a blockchain? Because a normal database always has an owner, who can change the numbers or pay anyone.
On a blockchain, the rules are public code. Nobody can override them, and anyone can check every transfer.
No middleman holding the money. Just rules that nobody can bend.
This is Earmark.

This is... Earmark.
